standard_prerequisites.name: Ergodicity of an interval exchange transformation
standard_prerequisites.statement: The transformation is ergodic with respect to Lebesgue measure, so it has no non-trivial invariant union of intervals.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the hypothesis of the statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: Connection time
standard_prerequisites.statement: M(beta) is the first return time of the left endpoint of the subinterval beta to the set of discontinuities, possibly infinite.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the quantity whose finiteness is excluded.

standard_prerequisites.name: Periodic behaviour from finite connection times
standard_prerequisites.statement: If all connection times except one are finite, the transformation has a finite decomposition into periodic components.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the contradiction derived in the proof.

core_obligations: Assume ergodicity together with the negation of the conclusion, so that every connection time except the excluded one is finite (source line 225).
Apply the criterion that finite connection times force a decomposition of the interval into finitely many semi-closed periodic components (source line 225).
Derive the contradiction with ergodicity, since such a decomposition is a non-trivial invariant decomposition (source line 225).

proof_roadmap.step: Negate the conclusion and apply the periodic-behaviour criterion.
Confront the resulting invariant decomposition with ergodicity.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled corollary at source lines 220-222: an ergodic interval exchange transformation has a connection time equal to infinity. The proof (source lines 224-226) is a contradiction argument whose whole force comes from reading the preceding criterion correctly: the negated conclusion supplies finiteness of the connection times, the criterion then produces a finite decomposition of the interval into semi-closed periodic components, and it is the ergodicity hypothesis that this decomposition contradicts, since such a decomposition is invariant and non-trivial. The statement records only the existence of an infinite connection time and neither the criterion applied nor the invariance of the decomposition.
